name: recruitment-adaptive
title: Adaptive receptor recruitment: fold-change detection across background cue levels
question:
Across a RANGE of background cue levels -- not just one -- can responders
keep being recruited to a rising source cue? Fold-change detection
(fold_change_detection) predicts that an adaptive receptor mechanism, which
re-centers its half-occupancy point on the locally sensed mean rather than
fixing it, should recruit at both low and high static backgrounds, while a
fixed-kd (hill_occupancy) mechanism saturates and collapses once the
background rises far enough to pin occupancy near its ceiling on both sides
of the gradient. This study is the LOCKED CONTRACT: it does not itself run
the model -- it defines the behavior-test bands the model-building loop
(Task 7) must clear for "the adaptive model works" to be true.
hypothesis:
An adaptive receptor mechanism (a slowly-tracked local-mean set-point that
re-centers the Hill kd every SAMPLE-step increment) recruits responders at
low background AND at high background, because it senses the CHANGE in
local occupancy rather than its absolute level (Barkai & Leibler 1997;
Tu, Shimizu & Berg 2008). A fixed-kd hill mechanism recruits at low
background but collapses at high background once both sides of the
gradient saturate near occupancy ceiling. Both mechanisms are abolished
when the downstream chemotactic response is blocked, since neither is a
metric artifact -- only a mechanism that isn't receptor-mediated at all
(the static-lambda control) would ignore that block.
objective:
Author the acceptance contract for the adaptive-receptor rung of the
faithful chemotaxis mechanism ladder (pbg_cpm_studies.model_building.
mechanisms): three primary behavior tests plus a receptor-gating control,
with pass/fail bands set from real measured recruitment_index values
(3-12 seeds) already gathered while calibrating the ladder. The loop
driver built in the next task runs mechanisms.simulate_condition against
these bands; this study does not itself constitute a completed run.
description:
This is the LOCKED CONTRACT study for the adaptive rung of the
recruitment-model-building faithful mechanism ladder (static_lambda ->
hill_occupancy -> adaptive_receptor). The ladder is built and calibrated:
static recruits at every background (it is not receptor-mediated, so the
background cancels out of the chemotaxis bias exactly); hill_occupancy
recruits at low background but collapses once a high uniform background
saturates receptor occupancy on both sides of the local gradient; and
adaptive_receptor rescues recruitment at high background by re-centering
its effective kd on the locally sensed mean every SAMPLE-step increment,
so it detects the FOLD CHANGE (the rise) in local concentration rather than
its absolute level. This study authors the behavior_tests that make "the
adaptive model works" falsifiable and locked BEFORE the loop is driven
against it: recruitment at low background, recruitment at high background
(the discriminating test -- only the adaptive mechanism passes; hill
collapses to 0), and receptor gating (blocking the response abolishes
recruitment for both receptor-gated mechanisms, but NOT for the
non-receptor-mediated static mechanism, which is the discriminating
knockout the loop must climb past). `conditions.baseline.composite`
points at the real, registered base recruitment world
(pbg_cpm_studies.composites.chemotaxis.recruitment -- source secretion +
responder chemotaxis, shared by all three ladder mechanisms); the
adaptive_receptor mechanism itself (kd/hill/epsilon) is what the loop
INSTALLS on top of that base world, documented under
`conditions.model_settings` rather than as baseline params, since it
directly manipulates the Rust CPM engine's chemotaxis-occupancy API
(world.set_chemotaxis_occupancy + a per-increment adaptation update)
rather than being its own registered @composite_generator. The actual
runner the loop drives is
mechanisms.simulate_condition("adaptive_receptor", condition, seeds,
steps) (see key_assumptions / model_change).
claim:
A receptor mechanism that adapts its half-occupancy set-point to the
locally sensed background (fold-change detection) recruits responders
across a RANGE of background cue levels where a fixed-kd mechanism
saturates and fails: measured recruitment_index at low_bg is 0.82
(adaptive) vs 0.58 (hill); at high_bg it is ~0.56 (adaptive, mean over 12
seeds) vs 0.00 (hill, deterministic collapse). Blocking the receptor-gated
response abolishes recruitment for both (0.00), while the non-receptor
static mechanism ignores the block (0.72) -- the discriminating control
that isolates receptor-mediated gating as the necessary cause.

purpose.question:
Across a range of background cue levels (fold_change_detection), does an
adaptive receptor mechanism keep recruiting responders to a rising
source cue where a fixed-kd mechanism saturates and collapses?

sourcing.rationale: receptor occupancy is catalogued; adaptation is composed on top via occupancy-space chemotaxis with an adaptive kd

model_settings.name: occupancy_chemotaxis
model_settings.note: The adaptive mechanism the loop installs on the base world: occupancy-space chemotaxis (Rust set_chemotaxis_occupancy) with an adaptive kd that tracks the local mean concentration. Params kd=1.0, hill=4.0, epsilon=0.5. Run via pbg_cpm_studies.model_building.mechanisms.simulate_condition("adaptive_receptor", ...).

readouts.name: Recruitment index
readouts.description: Fraction of responder cell centres of mass within the recruitment radius of the source centroid, read off the final live world after mechanisms.simulate_condition's SAMPLE-step run increments.

readouts.name: Responder mean distance
readouts.description: Mean centre-of-mass distance from responders to the source centroid, the distance-based complement to recruitment_index.

behavior_tests.name: recruits_low
behavior_tests.description: Pass criterion: recruitment index in [0.4, 1.0] at low background (background=0.0). Measured: adaptive 0.82, hill 0.58 (both mechanisms recruit at low background -- this test establishes baseline competence, not discrimination; recruits_high is the discriminator).

behavior_tests.name: receptor_gating
behavior_tests.description: Pass criterion: recruitment index <= 0.15 at high_bg_blocked (background=400.0, blocked=True -- the activated-type chemotaxis lambda forced to 0 downstream of receptor occupancy). Measured: hill/adaptive 0.00 (response blocked, receptor-mediated recruitment abolished); static 0.72 (ignores the block -- it is not receptor-mediated, so it FAILS this test, isolating receptor-gated response as the necessary cause).

behavior_tests.name: recruits_high
behavior_tests.description: Pass criterion: recruitment index in [0.35, 1.0] at high background (background=400.0). THE DISCRIMINATING TEST -- fold-change detection: measured adaptive ~0.56 (mean over 12 seeds) PASSES; hill_occupancy 0.00 (deterministic collapse, occupancy saturated on both sides of the gradient) FAILS. Only the adaptive mechanism clears this band.

controls.name: Receptor gating (response blocked downstream of receptor occupancy)
controls.description: With the cue present at a high background (400.0) but the activated-type chemotaxis lambda forced to 0 (blocked=True), both receptor-gated mechanisms (hill_occupancy and adaptive_receptor) fall to recruitment_index 0.00 -- receptor-mediated recruitment is abolished. The non-receptor static_lambda mechanism ignores the block (0.72), because its chemotaxis bias is a raw field-difference term unaffected by occupancy gating -- isolating receptor-mediated response as this test's discriminator, and static_lambda as a designed FAIL case for it.

controls.name: Fixed-kd hill mechanism is the discriminating knockout
controls.description: hill_occupancy is not a negative control on the world (the cue and response are both present and receptor-gated) -- it is the DISCRIMINATING KNOCKOUT the loop must climb past: a receptor mechanism with the same Hill machinery as adaptive_receptor but a FIXED kd collapses to recruitment_index 0.00 at high background because occupancy saturates near its ceiling on both sides of the local gradient, erasing the signal the chemotaxis bias needs. Only adding adaptation (a tracked, re-centering kd_eff) rescues recruitment (~0.56). A loop-built model that reuses hill_occupancy's fixed-kd machinery without adaptation will fail recruits_high by design.

key_assumptions: Measured bands are set from 3-12 seed means gathered during faithful mechanism-ladder calibration (docs/superpowers/notes/ 2026-08-18-faithful-ladder-calibration.md), not from a canonical run of THIS study -- status is in-progress / phase Build because the loop (Task 7) has not yet been driven against this locked contract.

`conditions.baseline.composite` is the real, registered base recruitment world (pbg_cpm_studies.composites.chemotaxis.recruitment) shared by all three ladder mechanisms (static_lambda / hill_occupancy / adaptive_receptor); its params are only what that generator accepts (cue_rate, chemo_lambda). The adaptive_receptor mechanism itself (kd/hill/epsilon) is what the loop INSTALLS on top of that base world -- it is not a resolvable @composite_generator on its own, since mechanisms.py drives the Rust CPM engine's chemotaxis-occupancy API directly (world.set_chemotaxis_occupancy + a per-increment adaptation update) rather than assembling a separate process_bigraph Composite document -- so those params live under conditions.model_settings as documentation. The loop driver runs it via mechanisms.simulate_condition(mechanism="adaptive_receptor", condition, seeds, steps), reading kd/hill/epsilon from conditions.model_settings[0].params.

low_bg / high_bg / high_bg_blocked are entries of mechanisms.CONDITIONS (background 0.0 / 400.0 / 400.0+blocked), not separate study conditions -- behavior_tests[].measure.condition names the CONDITIONS key the loop driver passes to simulate_condition, not a study slug.

recruits_low's band [0.4, 1.0] is intentionally non-discriminating (both adaptive 0.82 and hill 0.58 clear it) -- it exists to confirm baseline chemotactic competence before recruits_high does the actual discriminating work between the fixed-kd and adaptive mechanisms.

model_change.notes: Not yet realized as a run under this study -- the contract documents the adaptive_receptor arm of pbg_cpm_studies.model_building.mechanisms, which layers an adaptive kd_eff tracking update on top of the existing chemotaxis-occupancy bias (world.set_chemotaxis_occupancy), itself built on the chemotaxis.recruitment world (source secretion + responder chemotaxis). No new CPMProcess or listener was added; the mechanism reconfigures the existing engine's per-type chemotaxis parameters between SAMPLE-step run increments.

conclusion:
DECIDED -- PASS. The model-building loop (scripts/build_recruitment_loop.py)
was driven against this locked 3-test contract and climbed the faithful
mechanism ladder emergently, NOT by script: starting from static_lambda it
read the graded behavior tests each iteration and installed the mechanism
the most-negative failing margin demanded. iter 0 static_lambda fails
receptor_gating (0.69 > 0.15 -- not receptor-mediated, ignores the block)
-> install hill_occupancy; iter 1 hill_occupancy fails recruits_high (0.00 --
fixed-kd occupancy saturates on both sides of the gradient at high
background) -> install adaptive_receptor; iter 2 adaptive_receptor clears all
three (recruits_low 0.9167 in [0.4,1.0]; receptor_gating 0.00 <= 0.15;
recruits_high 0.7222 in [0.35,1.0]) -> DONE in 3 iterations, violations=[].
The pass is perturbation-stable: re-grading adaptive_receptor at a fully
disjoint 6-seed set (7,53,71,89,101,113) clears all three again. A GIVE_UP
companion run with adaptive_receptor withheld from the library terminates
HONESTLY at hill_occupancy rather than faking a pass. Fold-change detection
(Barkai & Leibler 1997; Tu, Shimizu & Berg 2008) is therefore sufficient, on
the real Rust CPM engine, to keep recruiting responders across a range of
background cue levels where a fixed-kd receptor mechanism collapses. Full
emergent trajectory + audit/lock/perturbation/give-up traces:
../../investigations/chemotactic-recruitment/trajectory.json (schema
model_build_trajectory/v2); loop state: .pbg/loop/recruitment-adaptive.json.
